text: Five students A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. B is at the left end. D is at the right end. A is next to B. C is next to D. Who sits in the middle?
explanation: The row from left to right is B, A, then the middle, then C, D. The only student left is E, so E is in the middle.

text: Six people sit in a row facing north. P is third from the left and Q is second from the right. How many people sit between P and Q?
explanation: Number the seats 1 to 6 from the left. P is in seat 3, and Q second from the right is in seat 5. Only seat 4 lies between them, so 1 person. Counting the endpoints themselves is what turns this into 3.

text: Four friends sit around a square table, one to a side, facing the centre. Ravi is opposite Sita. Meena is to the immediate left of Ravi. Who is opposite Meena?
explanation: Ravi and Sita take two opposite sides, leaving the other two sides for Meena and Arun, who must therefore be opposite each other. So Arun is opposite Meena, and the extra detail about Meena's position does not change it.

text: Five students sit in a row facing north: the tallest is in the middle, the two shortest at the two ends. If A is tallest and E and D are the two shortest, who can sit second from the left?
options: B or C|A only|D or E|B only
explanation: A takes the middle seat and D and E take the two ends, so the two remaining seats -- second from the left and second from the right -- belong to B and C in either order. So B or C.

text: Eight people sit around a circular table facing the centre. If R is fourth to the left of S, how many places is R to the right of S?
explanation: Around a table of eight, going one way four places and going the other way four places reach the same seat, because 8 - 4 = 4. So R is also fourth to the right of S. This only happens when the gap is exactly half the table.

text: Seven students sit in a row facing north. G sits in the middle and F is immediately to the right of G. What is F's position counted from the right end?
explanation: In a row of seven the middle is seat 4, so G is in seat 4 and F in seat 5. From the right, seat 5 is the 3rd (seats 7, 6, 5). Counting from the wrong end is the only difficulty here, which is why the question names the end it wants.

text: Six people sit in a row facing SOUTH. If X is third from the left end of the row as the observer sees it, what is X's position from the left of the people themselves?
explanation: People facing south have their left where the observer's right is. Third from the observer's left is fourth from their right in a row of six, which is their own left. So X is 4th from their own left. Direction of facing is the whole question in these items.

text: Five people sit around a circular table facing the centre: A, B, C, D and E in clockwise order. Who is to the immediate left of C?
explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the ANTICLOCKWISE direction. Going anticlockwise from C in the order A, B, C, D, E reaches B. The usual error is to read clockwise and answer D.

text: Three students scored 72, 85 and 91 in a test, in some order. Ravi did not score the highest. Sita scored more than Ravi. Meena scored 72. What did Ravi score?
explanation: Meena took 72, so Ravi and Sita hold 85 and 91. Ravi did not score the highest, so Ravi has 85 and Sita 91. Both clues about Ravi point the same way, which is how a well-formed puzzle closes.

text: Four students take four different electives: cloud, security, data and graphics. A does not take cloud or data. B takes security. C does not take graphics. Which elective does A take?
explanation: B has security, so A is left with graphics (cloud and data are ruled out for A by the first clue). C then takes cloud or data, and D the other, which the question does not ask.

text: A cube of side 3 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have no paint at all?
explanation: Only the cube at the very centre is enclosed on every side: the inner block measures (3-2) cubed = 1. The 8 corner cubes have three faces painted, the 12 edge cubes two, and the 6 face centres one.

text: A clock loses 5 minutes every hour. It is set correctly at 6 a.m. What will it show when the correct time is 12 noon?
explanation: Six hours pass, and the clock loses 5 minutes in each: 30 minutes lost in all. So it shows 12:00 less 30 minutes = 11:30 a.m.

text: In a group of 40 students, 24 play cricket, 18 play football and 6 play neither. How many play both?
explanation: Students playing at least one game: 40 - 6 = 34. Cricket and football counts add to 42, so the overlap is 42 - 34 = 8. Adding the two counts and subtracting the total without removing the 'neither' group is the standard slip.

text: A, B and C contribute Rs 6,000, Rs 4,000 and Rs 2,000 to a project and share a profit of Rs 3,600 in proportion to their contributions. What does B receive?
explanation: The contributions are in the ratio 3:2:1, which is six parts. One part of 3,600 is 600, so B's two parts are 1,200. (A gets 1,800 and C gets 600, which are the distractors.)

text: A water tank is one-fifth full. After 30 litres are added it is half full. What is the tank's capacity?
explanation: The 30 litres filled the gap between a fifth and a half, which is 3/10 of the tank. So the capacity is 30 x 10/3 = 100 litres. (Check: a fifth is 20 litres, plus 30 gives 50, which is half of 100.)

text: Three taps fill a tank in 20, 30 and 60 minutes. All three are opened together, and the third is closed after 5 minutes. How long does the tank take to fill in total?
explanation: Per minute the taps give 3/60, 2/60 and 1/60, so all three together give 6/60 = 1/10 of the tank. In 5 minutes they fill half of it. The remaining half runs on the first two at 5/60 = 1/12 a minute, taking 6 minutes. Total 5 + 6 = 11 minutes.

text: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is she related to Ravi?
explanation: The grandfather's only son is Ravi's father, so the girl is his father's daughter: his sister. 'Only son' is the clue that closes it -- with more than one son she could have been a cousin.

text: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
explanation: C is the mother of B and of B's sister A, and D is C's father, so D is A's grandfather and A is his granddaughter.

text: Introducing a man, a woman said, 'His wife is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to the woman?
explanation: The only daughter of her mother is the woman herself, so the man's wife is the speaker: he is her husband. The phrase to hold on to is 'only daughter', which rules out a sister.

text: P is the brother of Q. R is the father of P. S is the sister of R. How is S related to Q?
explanation: R is the father of both P and Q, and S is R's sister, so S is the father's sister, which makes her aunt to Q: her aunt.

text: X is the son of Y. Z is the mother of Y. W is the husband of Z. How is W related to X?
explanation: Z is X's grandmother, because she is the mother of X's parent Y. W is Z's husband, so W is his grandfather -- one generation above Y, not two.

text: A and B are sisters. C is the son of A. D is the daughter of B. How are C and D related?
options: Cousins|Brother and sister|Uncle and niece|Cannot be determined
explanation: C and D have mothers who are sisters, so they are the children of two siblings: cousins. They cannot be brother and sister, because their mothers are different people.

text: A student walks 3 km north, then 4 km east. How far is she from her starting point?
explanation: North and east are at right angles, so the distance is the hypotenuse: the square root of 9 + 16 = 25, which is 5 km. Adding the legs gives 7, which is the distance walked and not the distance away.

text: Facing north, a person turns 90 degrees clockwise, then 180 degrees. Which direction is he facing?
explanation: Ninety degrees clockwise from north is east; a further 180 degrees is west. Turning the same total anticlockwise would end at east, which is the distractor.

text: A car travels 6 km south, 8 km west, then 6 km north. How far is it from where it started, and in which direction?
options: 8 km west|10 km west|8 km south|20 km west
explanation: The 6 km south and 6 km north cancel, leaving the 8 km west. The answer is 8 km west. The 10 km option is the hypotenuse of 6 and 8, which would be right if the car had not come back north.

text: Walking towards the setting sun, a student turns to her right and walks 5 km, then turns right again. Which direction is she now walking?
explanation: The sun sets in the west, so she begins walking west. A right turn faces her north, and a second right turn faces her east.

text: A person walks 10 m north, 6 m east, 2 m south and 6 m west. How far is he from the start?
explanation: East 6 and west 6 cancel. North 10 and south 2 leave 8 m north. So he is 8 m from the start. Tracking the two axes separately is the only reliable method once a path has more than two legs.

text: At 9 a.m. a pole's shadow falls towards the west. A student walks along the shadow away from the pole, then turns left. Which direction is she facing?
explanation: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows fall west; walking away from the pole she walks west. Facing west, her left hand points south, so after turning left she faces south.
